actor: MCP specification maintainer / core spec editor
job: Drafting the next official MCP spec revision, promoting remote-transport authentication and caller identity from SHOULD/OPTIONAL guidance to a normative MUST
outcome: A dated, published spec revision that makes auth or a verified identity/authorization handshake a MUST for remote/HTTP-transport servers
motivation: Optional SHOULD-grade guidance produced a population of unauthenticated public servers; only a normative MUST closes the gap durably

task.who: MCP spec working group / maintainers and security-focused contributors
task.what: Revise transport spec to require remote-server authentication
task.where: MCP specification repository, RFC/proposal and review process
task.why: Optional guidance left public servers unauthenticated by default
task.how: Normative MUST language in a dated spec revision / RFC

job: Sweeping public MCP repositories and internet-exposed servers, disclosing zero-days, CVEs, and broken-OAuth flows that quantify the unauthenticated-server problem
outcome: Published scans and CVE disclosures (VIPER-MCP, Censys, no-auth studies) that pressure maintainers to mandate auth at the spec level
motivation: Demonstrating that ~40% of remote servers expose tools with no auth makes per-server fixes look inadequate versus a structural one

task.who: External security research teams (scanner vendors, academic studies)
task.what: Scan MCP servers and disclose auth/OAuth vulnerabilities
task.where: Public MCP repos, internet-accessible MCP services, CVE databases
task.why: Quantified exposure forces a spec-level rather than per-server fix
task.how: Automated MCP scanners (VIPER-MCP-class), CVE disclosure process

actor: government zero-trust guidance author (NSA design-considerations track)
job: Publishing and extending a government baseline that names inverted client-server, unverified task propagation, tool-poisoning, and arbitrary-code-execution as core MCP risks
outcome: Authoritative guidance establishing authenticate-every-remote-server as the expected baseline that the spec is pressured to encode normatively
motivation: A government zero-trust baseline gives maintainers cover and external pressure to move auth from optional to mandatory

task.who: National-security / cyber agency guidance authors and reviewers
task.what: Publish design-considerations baseline mandating remote-server auth
task.where: Agency design-considerations and zero-trust guidance documents
task.why: Set authenticate-by-default as the expected protocol baseline
task.how: Zero-trust design-considerations document and follow-on guidance
